newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN C.BANK NO COMMENT ON INTERVENTION TALK.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN C.BANK NO COMMENT ON INTERVENTION TALK.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank declined to confirm or deny whether it had intervened to defend the Taiwan dollar following the dramatic local unit rebound on Thursday.
"No central bank in the world will tell you if there is any intervention," a central bank official told reporters.
"Go and ask the market," the official said.

Dealers said strong intervention orchestrated by the central bank in the final moments of Thursday's trade pulled the Taiwan dollar back from the brink of another nine-year low close, ensuring a slightly firmer finish.
The local dollar had tumbled to as low as T$28.970 in brisk late trade before rebounding to close at T$28.639, against Wednesday's T$28.656 finish.
The bank official said its attitude towards the foreign exchange market remained unchanged.
Taiwan's central bank announced on July 31 a modest tightening of monetary policy by raising two key rates in a bid to maintain forex market stability.
The bank has said it would leave the Taiwan dollar exchange rate at the mercy of market forces -- with one caveat.
"The central bank will respect market forces and let market supply and demand determine the Taiwan dollar exchange rates," central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said.
"But if there are abnormal factors intervening in the market it will adopt appropriate measures to maintain the foreign exchange market's stability," he said.
